concerns.text: Task T002 selects Qwen1.5-1.5B, but T012c and T013 implement an automatic fallback to Qwen1.5-0.5B if RAM > 7GB. Spec FR-002 mandates a '1.5B parameter model (or a heavily quantized 7B model)' for the baseline. A 0.5B model is not a valid substitute under FR-002. This task silently weakens the model-size constraint, violating Constitution Principle VI (Hardware-Agnostic Signal Validation) by introducing model-size-dependent bias into the ground truth.

Task T009b mandates raising a RuntimeError if memory > 90% instead of adapting batch size. Spec FR-007 requires processing in batches of 50 'to ensure memory usage remains within the 7 GB RAM limit'. Raising an error violates the 'ensure' constraint by making the process brittle and failing to guarantee the memory limit is respected under load, effectively weakening the safety guarantee of FR-007.

Tasks T030/T031 mandate Mixed-Effects Logistic Regression (GLMM) with random intercepts. Spec FR-004 requires 'logistic regression... stratified by task type... and pooling layers'. While GLMM is a valid statistical method, the spec does not authorize the added complexity of random effects (requiring `pymer4`) nor define how to handle the stratification within a GLMM framework. This introduces a methodological constraint not present in the spec, risking reproducibility if the GLMM fails to converge on the small dataset, which is a semantic weakening of the 'fit a logistic regression' requirement.

Task T051 implements a 'real sample' fallback (islice) if RAM > 7GB and sets a `sample_deviation` flag. Spec Assumptions state compute time will remain within CI/CD constraints. By implementing a fallback that admits the assumption might be violated without amending the spec's scope, this task silently relaxes the 'maximum of 500 examples' constraint of FR-001 to a 'variable sample size' constraint, weakening the data volume requirement.
